subject: ela
intro: Seventh graders analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or interpreting facts differently. Two authors may agree on the facts but disagree on what they mean, or may stress different details. Comparing them gives a fuller, more balanced understanding.

items.prompt:
Two articles report that a new factory will create 500 jobs. One emphasizes the jobs; the other emphasizes the pollution the factory will cause.

How do the authors SHAPE their presentations differently?

steps: Both agree on the facts (500 jobs) but stress different parts.
One emphasizes benefits (jobs); the other emphasizes costs (pollution).
So the authors shape their presentations by emphasizing different evidence.
solution.answer: One emphasizes the jobs (benefits); the other emphasizes the pollution (costs).

items.prompt:
Two historians agree a battle happened but interpret its importance differently.

What differs between them?

steps: They share the facts but differ on interpretation.
So they differ in how they interpret the facts' meaning.
solution.answer: Their interpretation of what the facts mean.

items.prompt: Why read MULTIPLE authors on the same topic?

steps: Each author emphasizes or interprets differently.
So reading several gives a fuller, more balanced understanding.
solution.answer: To get a fuller, more balanced understanding.

items.prompt: Two authors can agree on facts but differ on ____.
Reading several authors gives a more ____ view.
